question: Which Five year plan in India was based on P.C.Mahalanobis Model? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: 3rd Five Year Plan
1st Five Year Plan
4th Five Year Plan
2nd Five Year Plan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2nd Five Year Plan

Explanation:
India's Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961) was based on the P.C. Mahalanobis Model, developed by the renowned statistician Prashant Chandra Mahalanobis. This model emphasized the development of heavy industries and capital goods to boost long-term economic growth. The plan aimed to increase national income by 25%, while the first plan focused on agriculture and infrastructure. The Mahalanobis model used a two-sector model consisting of consumer goods and capital goods sectors. As a result of this plan, significant growth was achieved in steel, coal, and electricity production.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ What was the duration of the Second Five Year Plan? → 1956-1961
☛ What did the Mahalanobis Model emphasize? → Heavy industries
☛ What was the income growth target of the Second Plan? → 25%
☛ What was the main focus of the First Five Year Plan? → Agriculture
question_hi: भारत में कौन-सी पंचवर्षीय योजना पी. सी. महालनोबिस मॉडल पर आधारित थी? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/01/2021) Shift 1)

question: The purchasing power of a currency relative to another at current exchange rates and prices is _________. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: nominal exchange rate
real exchange rate
balance of payments
purchasing power parity
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is real exchange rate

Explanation:
The real exchange rate measures the relative purchasing power of two currencies at current exchange rates and price levels. It indicates how expensive a country's goods are compared to another's. It is calculated by multiplying the nominal exchange rate by the ratio of foreign to domestic price levels. While the nominal exchange rate simply reflects the current rate between currencies, the real exchange rate incorporates the effects of inflation. Purchasing power parity (PPP) is a theory that suggests in the long run, the real exchange rate should equal 1. The balance of payments is a broader concept that records all economic transactions between a country and the rest of the world.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Real exchange rate formula → (Nominal exchange rate × Foreign price level) / Domestic price level
☛ Nominal exchange rate → Current exchange rate between two currencies
☛ Purchasing power parity (PPP) → Makes real exchange rate equal to 1 in the long run
☛ Increase in real exchange rate → Domestic goods become more expensive for foreigners
☛ Balance of payments → Record of all economic transactions of a country
question_hi: वर्तमान विनिमय दरों और मूल्यों पर एक मुद्रा की दूसरी मुद्रा के सापेक्ष क्रय शक्ति _________ है। (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/01/2021) Shift 2)
options_hi: नाममात्र विनिमय दर
वास्तविक विनिमय दर
भुगतान संतुलन
क्रय शक्ति समता
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है वास्तविक विनिमय दर

Explanation:
वास्तविक विनिमय दर दो मुद्राओं के बीच सापेक्ष क्रय शक्ति को मापती है, जो वर्तमान विनिमय दरों और मूल्य स्तरों पर आधारित होती है। यह बताती है कि एक देश की वस्तुएं दूसरे देश की तुलना में कितनी महंगी या सस्ती हैं। इसे नाममात्र विनिमय दर को मूल्य स्तरों के अनुपात से गुणा करके निकाला जाता है। जबकि नाममात्र विनिमय दर केवल मुद्राओं की वर्तमान दर को दर्शाती है, वास्तविक विनिमय दर मुद्रास्फीति के प्रभाव को शामिल करती है। क्रय शक्ति समता (PPP) एक सिद्धांत है जो बताता है कि लंबे समय में वास्तविक विनिमय दर 1 के बराबर होनी चाहिए। भुगतान संतुलन एक व्यापक अवधारणा है जो देश के सभी आर्थिक लेन-देन को रिकॉर्ड करती है।

question: Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) is a _______ company.  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/01/2021) Shift 2)

Rajratna
Navratna
Miniratna
solution:

Explanation:

The Maharatna status is awarded by the Ministry of Finance to companies that are globally competitive and have an average net profit of over Rs. 5,000 crore in the last three years. BHEL is a leading manufacturer of heavy electrical equipment and is headquartered in New Delhi. The company was established in 1964 and manufactures equipment for power generation, transmission, and distribution.

question: Which of the following does NOT support rural development? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Promotion of organic farming
Development of marketing
Development of human resources
Urban credit
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Urban credit

Explanation:
Rural development aims at improving the economic and social conditions of rural areas. Promotion of organic farming increases farmers' income and protects the environment. In contrast, urban credit provides financial assistance in urban areas and does not directly contribute to the process of rural development. Hence, urban credit does not support rural development.

question: Who among the following calculated per capita income of India in 1867 and published in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule of India'? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Sir Arthur Cotton
Dadabhai Naoroji
Motilal Nehru
Lord Cornwallis
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dadabhai Naoroji

Explanation:
Dadabhai Naoroji calculated the per capita income of India in 1867 and published it in his famous book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule of India' (1901). He was the first person to estimate India's national income and exposed the poverty of India under British rule. He propounded the 'Drain Theory', explaining how Britain was draining India's wealth. He was a prominent leader of the Indian national movement and served three times as a member of the British Parliament. His book provided an ideological foundation for the Indian freedom struggle.

question: Bank rate is the interest rate at which: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (25/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: commercial banks lend money to the central bank
the central bank lends money to the commercial banks
the Government borrows from the central bank
the central bank borrows from the government
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is the central bank lends money to the commercial banks

Explanation:
Bank rate is the interest rate at which the central bank (RBI in India) provides short-term loans to commercial banks. It is a key monetary policy tool used to control money supply and inflation in the economy. An increase in the bank rate makes borrowing more expensive for commercial banks, leading to higher market interest rates and reduced money supply. Conversely, a decrease in the bank rate lowers borrowing costs and increases money supply. It differs from the repo rate, which applies to repurchase agreements involving securities. The bank rate is also known as the discount rate.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is bank rate? → The rate at which central bank lends to commercial banks
☛ Alternate name for bank rate? → Discount rate
☛ Difference between bank rate and repo rate? → Bank rate has no collateral, while repo rate involves securities
☛ Who sets bank rate in India? → Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
☛ Effect of increasing bank rate? → Reduces inflation and money supply

question: Dear money refers to money that is hard to obtain due to: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (29/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: high rate of interest
low rate of interest
inflation
depression
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is high rate of interest

Explanation:
Dear money refers to a situation where loans are available at high rates of interest, making borrowing expensive and difficult. This policy is adopted by central banks to control inflation and reduce money supply in the economy. High interest rates discourage borrowing and spending, leading to lower investment and economic activity. In contrast, cheap money is available at low interest rates. Inflation and depression are not causes of dear money but can be consequences or related conditions. Dear money is a tool of contractionary monetary policy used to cool down an overheating economy.

☛ Cheap money is associated with which policy? → Expansionary monetary policy
☛ Primary objective of dear money policy? → Controlling inflation

☛ Effect of dear money on economy? → Reduces investment and demand

question: Which one among the following is the Asia's first stock exchange? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (01/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Tokyo Stock Exchange

National Stock Exchnage
Bombay Stock Exchange
solution:

question: Which of the following does the work of linking all the ATMs in India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (02/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: National Institute of Banking and Management
Reserve Bank of India
Securities and Exchange Board of India
National Payments Corporation of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)

Explanation:
The work of linking all the ATMs in India is done by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). NPCI was established in 2008 by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Indian Banks' Association (IBA). It operates the National Financial Switch (NFS), which is India's largest ATM network. Through NFS, customers of any bank can transact at any other bank's ATM. NPCI also manages other payment systems like UPI, IMPS, RuPay cards, etc. Thus, NPCI facilitates ATM interoperability across India.

question: Who among the following was the first Indian Governor of the Reserve Bank of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/02/2021) Shift 1)

Raghuram Rajan
IG Patel
CD Deshmukh

Explanation:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on April 1, 1935. Its first governor was Sir Osborne Smith (1935-1937), who was British.
